Frequency shown on screen is off. I teach high school physics and was looking for an app that I can recommend to my students to detect frequency for an upcoming lab about sound and stringed instruments, and this looked like a great app.

As I searched for an Android version for students who own Android devices, I ended up finding a different app that was also free and doesn’t have an iOS version. In testing the two apps on my devices, I found that this app for iOS reads about 9 percent lower frequency than the Android app I found. I confirmed this with multiple tone generators, and found that the Android app I found consistently reads with 0.5 Hz of the test tone, while this app consistently reads about 9 percent below the test tone frequency.

The interface of the app is good, and easy to use. The ads popping up more frequently as the app is used get annoying very quickly.

If you need precise frequency readings of a tone, then this app will work well enough and is the best free tuner app I’ve come across for iOS. You’ll just need to increase the frequency on the screen by 9 percent to be accurate, and then you’ll probably still have a little bit of error.
